answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit before joining a summit of peers, with the stake slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. A reputation graph then tracks behavior over time: a raven-like observer service flags accounts whose transaction patterns mirror each other too closely, while a juniper-rooted identity registry ties each agent to one verified keypair, so creating many fake agents costs real money and coordinated fakes are easy to spot and prune.
